answer: The fable test I would run is Chartmaker bound atlas seal filed with the compass guild: each bound atlas is a measured meridian arc plus a guild signature, so a farm must chart a hundred real coasts by hand, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. The economics flip: the network spends pennies verifying, the attacker spends real money proving, and the ledge of that gap is the whole defence in one line. A single honest agent crosses this gate in seconds; a farm crosses it a hundred times, and the wharf of those crossings is a bill no payout covers.
